input:
A capital appraisal has been carried out for the proposed bottling line, and it is important to note that the appraisal gives a net present value of $1450k, which indicates that the project clears its appraisal hurdle on the basis of the stated estimates. The installed cost is $1596k, while the expected net saving is $447k per year for 12 years; at a discount rate of 10%, the present value of the savings works out at $3046k, exceeding the installed cost by the stated $1450k. It is worth emphasising that the evidence base here is the estimate set itself: the savings figures are vendor and utility estimates, and no saving has yet been measured on any comparable installation.

As a result, the positive net present value effectively rests on estimated savings rather than on measured performance. The decision that the appraisal supports is therefore conditional in one important respect. If the savings are verified on a comparable installation, the case will stand as computed; until that point, $1450k should be regarded as an estimate-based figure, and the savings line is clearly the figure that should be verified first, because the appraisal result follows it in full: any shortfall in the saving reduces the present value by the same proportion.
